full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J:- This rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 9.11.98 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge Court No. 1, Pabna in Criminal Appeal No. 37 of 1988 allowing the Government Appeal on setting aside the judgment and order dated 25.4.1988 passed by the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, in Sathia Thana Case No. 64 dated 23.5.1986, acquitting all the accused persons of the charge levelled against them. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that at about 3.00 p.m. on 21.5.1986 the accused petitioner and others by forming an unlawful assembly illegally trespassed into the house of informant Md. Motleb Hossain and started forcibly plumping mangoes from a standing tree despite the protest of the inmates of the house. On the order of accused petitioner Kazi Azam, accused Rajab Ali inflicted a Hashua blow on the head of Kajal Bibi, sister of the informant, causing a grievous bleeding injury. Other accused persons also variously assaulted informant's wife Champa, and bhatiji Rowshanara, causing multiple injuries on their persons. The accused persons also assaulted informant brother Motin on various parts of the body. Injured Kajal Bibi was immediately taken to the local Government Hospital where she was treated before about 18 days. 

 3. The police after usual investigation submitted charge sheet against the 8 accused persons under sections 323/325./324/32/379 of the Penal Code to stand trial before the Court. Upon the aforesaid allegations, the accused persons were put on trial before the learned Magistrate, Sathia in G.R. Case No. 33 of 1996 to answer charges under section 447/323/325/342/379 of the Penal Code, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined as many as 13 witnesses, including the doctor who treated victim Kajal Bibi, in support of its case while the defence examined none. 

 12. The learned advocate appearing for the accused petitioner has placed before me the impugned judgments passed by the learned Courts below. It appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, on elaborate discussion and proper appreciation of the evidence on record, found the accused petitioner guilty under sections 448/447 of the penal Code. The learned Additional Sessions Judge also found the accused petitioner guilty under sections 325/109 of the Penal Code and sentenced him thereunder to suffer R.I. for 3 years and to pay a fine of Tk. 1,000.00, It is found from the evidence that except the passing of the so-called order, accused petitioner Kazi Azam did not do any other overt act in assaulting any of the inmates of the house of the informant. In the facts of the case, the passing of the order for assaulting the inmates of the house appears to be totally unnecessary. I also find want of uniformity in the evidence of the witnesses regarding the passing of order by accused petitioner Kazi Azam. 

 13. In our country there is usually a tendency on the part of the prosecution to rope in as many people of the enemy camp and possible in a case of factional feuds and to assign rules to the leading man of the accused party for passing an unnecessary order for starting assaults to be carried out by others. When the accused being fully armed comes to the place of the occurrence with a determination to carry out their preconcerted mission by the might of their muscle, the passing of an order by the head man of the party to start assaulting the opponent appears to be utterly superfluous and irrelevant. In many cases, this assaulting role is resigned to the elderly man of the accused party to entangle him in the case as on accused although he might not be present at the spot at all, just for giving him a bad name and for crippling the defence for want of proper prosecution. In such cases, the passing of the order for assaults by the leading man of the party is often a hoax and it is mischievously concocted to implicate the leading man of the accused party in the case, no matter whether he was present or not at the place of the occurrence. Of course, this is not to say that giving of "হুকুম" by the leading man of the accused party is always a concoction. There may be cases where the leading man of the accused party passed the order to carry out assaults by his men in his effort to encourage the members of his party and to bloater up their morale run into action forthwith. In such a case, he certainly comes with the mischief of the offence of abatement as being the instigator. At any rate, the Court shall have to decide the question of "হুকুম" in the light of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record and no inflexible rule of caution should be laid down on this score. In the instant case, the passing of the order by accused petitioner Kazi Azam for starting assaults accused petitioner appears to be totally superfluous and unnecessary and, consequently, he must be absolved of the ability of giving the “হুকুম".
